stem: What role do executive and management champions play in an organizational accessibility program?

options.text: They ensure accessibility is managed by a single dedicated team with clear central accountability.
options.shortLabel: Centralized dedicated team with clear accountability
options.rationale: Champions work to embed accessibility across functions; concentrating ownership in one team can create silos and is not their defining contribution.

options.text: They approve the annual accessibility budget and delegate strategy and prioritization to technical teams.
options.rationale: Budget approval and delegated strategy do not provide the vision, sustained commitment, and cross-organizational integration that champions contribute.

options.text: They build a shared vision, sustain commitment, and embed accessibility in organizational processes.
options.shortLabel: Build vision, sustain commitment, embed accessibility
options.rationale: Management champions build a shared vision, sustain ongoing commitment and collaboration, and support the programmatic integration of accessibility throughout organizational processes.

options.text: They coordinate external audits, manage regulatory inquiries, and report compliance status to leadership.
options.rationale: Audit coordination and compliance reporting are operational tasks; champions operate at a strategic and cultural level.

explanation: Executive and management champions act as visible advocates and role models within an organization. They help build a shared vision and align implementation strategies, sustain ongoing commitment and collaboration, and support the programmatic integration of accessibility throughout organizational processes. They also help lead adoption of an accessibility maturity model, so accessibility is managed as an enduring program rather than an isolated project.
